title: Agape
text:
Today no one has come to ask;

nor have they asked anything of me this afternoon.


I have not seen a single cemetery flower

in so joyful a procession of lights.

Forgive me, Lord: how little I have died!


This afternoon everyone, everyone passes by

without asking me or asking anything of me.


And I do not know what they forget, and it remains

wrong in my hands, like something alien.


I have gone out to the door,

and I feel like shouting to everyone:

If you are missing something, it is left here!


Because on every afternoon of this life,

I do not know with what doors they strike a face,

and something alien takes over my soul.


Today no one has come;

and today, how little I have died this afternoon!
editorial_note: The translation keeps Vallejo's paradox of unclaimed loss: something alien remains, and yet he has died only a little.

title: Trilce: Poem LXXIV - There Was So Rich a Day Last Year...
text:
There was so rich a day last year...!

that now I do not even know what to do with it.


Severe mothers, guides to school,

besiege reflections, and we arrow

our faces barely. Only late to know

that in that mischief hinges

and the temple breaks.

What a day, that one last year,

that now I do not even know what to do with it,

the temple broken and everything.


For this they will separate us,

for that and so we will no longer do harm.

And the technical reflections still say,

will you not hear them?,

that inside two dark graph-lines and apart,

for having been children and also

for having joined too much in life,

they will lock us up, prisoners forever.


So that you may put yourself together.
editorial_note: The translation preserves Vallejo's fractured school, childhood, and confinement imagery, including 'graph-lines' for gráfilas.

title: Between Pain and Pleasure Stand Three Creatures
text:
Between pain and pleasure stand three creatures,

of whom one looks at a wall,

the second makes use of a sad spirit,

and the third advances on tiptoe;

but, between you and me,

only second creatures exist.


Leaning on my forehead, the day

agrees that, truly,

there is much exactness in space;

but if happiness, which after all has a size,

begins, alas, with my mouth,

who will ask me about my word?


To the instantaneous sense of eternity

there corresponds

this meeting invested with black thread,

but to your temporal farewell

there corresponds only the immutable,

your creature, the soul, my word.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's abstract creatures, exact space, black thread, and word-soul ending.

title: Naked in Clay
text:
Like horrible batrachians toward the atmosphere,

lugubrious grimaces rise to the lip.

Through the blue Sahara of Substance

a gray verse walks, a dromedary.


A pout of cruel dreams phosphoresces.

And the blind man who died filled with voices

of snow. And to rise early, poet, nomad,

to the rawest day of being man.


The Hours go feverish, and in the angles

blond centuries of fortune miscarry.

Who pulls the thread so much: who lowers

without pity our nerves,

cords already worn, to the tomb!


Love! And you too. Black stones

are begotten in your mask and break it.

The tomb is still

a woman's sex that draws man on!
editorial_note: The translation keeps Vallejo's fierce surreal imagery: batrachians, Substance, worn nerves, and the erotic tomb.

title: Black Stone on a White Stone
text:
I will die in Paris in a downpour,

        on a day I already remember.

        I will die in Paris-and I do not run away-

        perhaps on a Thursday, as today is, in autumn.


        It will be Thursday, because today, Thursday, as I prose

        these verses, I have set my humeri

        badly, and never as today have I turned,

        with all my road, to see myself alone.


        César Vallejo has died; they beat him,

        all of them, though he did nothing to them;

        they struck him hard with a stick and hard


        also with a rope; witnesses are

        the Thursdays and the humerus bones,

        solitude, rain, roads...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the famous self-elegy's Thursday, rain, humeri, and third-person death.
